_burial:
A station is called buried when its signed distance to the nearest skin triangle is negative. Two facts, measured across the population.

The per-vertex identity changes nothing here: every subject within a tenth of a percentage point and two tenths of a millimetre, none worse. The seats ride the surface as the schema intends.

The absolute share does hold a real defect. A median of 28% of stations are under the skin, and eight to twenty-four per cent of them are more than ten millimetres under, sitting at the crown — that is hair inside the skull rather than hair touching it, because a lock lying on a cheek or a shoulder is a millimetre or two under. It predates the identity layer and comes from the transfer: these locks were authored on the procedural head and re-seated on the connected one, so wherever the connected skull is the larger of the two, a station that kept its authored height ended up underneath.
_burialRepairRejected:
Lifting each buried station out along the surface normal was built, measured and rejected on the render twice.

Station by station it took the burial from 28.3% to 0.2% and every subject to zero beyond ten millimetres — and the hair came back in spikes and tears, because a guide is a curve and moving one station sixty millimetres past its neighbour is a kink.

Smoothing the displacement along the lock fixed the tearing and reached 15.3% overall with ten-millimetre burial at 0.5 to 2.5%. That render is still worse than no repair at all: the crowns of daniel-radcliffe, lee-tae-ri, park-eun-bin, rupert-grint and maggie-smith come back rough where they were smooth.

Both were reverted. The buried segments were hidden, and exposing them shows geometry authored for a different head. What this asks for is re-seating the locks against the connected scalp at authoring time, not pushing the authored ones outward afterwards. The tools are in .shots/human-2469/investigation-2498: measure-burial-depth.py and apply-groom-clearance.ts.
